event: Nala says killing for pay suits her, but asks what else the oath holds; she values her freedom.
Varne sets down her pen. "Three things: keep the margrave's peace, answer my call, speak true."
"My call is against outlaws and beasts, paid at the Board's rates, as I said."
"Speaking true means when I ask what you've seen on my roads, you tell me straight."
"Otherwise you go where you like and hunt for whom you like, in Wendlow or far past it."
"You may turn a call down if you give this bench your reason. Ignore one, and the oath is broken."
"A broken oath voids the papers and strikes your name; you're simply a stranger again."
"And you may hand your papers back before this bench any day you like, and be quit of it."
"One more, since you ask. In war the margrave may summon the march's sworn hunters."
"So far in this war he's left us be. That may change."
"The letter bargain stands apart from the oath, whatever you choose."
"I've written the margrave three times for riders to clear the east road. Three times, refused."
"So you know where you stand: swear, and the east road is my first call on you."
